body.statement: For every \(k\ge0\) and \(n\ge2k+4\), \(d_{e^{\star}}(G^{\star}_{k,n})=2^{k+1}\) and therefore \[D_k(n)=2^{k+1}.\] One original coefficient \(e^{\star}\) separates all branches on a nonempty Zariski-open covariance set.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(d=k+1\) and \(N=2d+2=2k+4\).  In the \(N\)-vertex member of \(\mathrm{def:attaining\mbox{-}family}\), the directed arrows are
\[
 0\to P_i,\qquad 0\to Q_i,\qquad P_i\to h
 \quad(1\le i\le d).
\]
The supplied set contains the first \(2d\) arrows and \(P_1\to h\).  Consequently
\[
 |T|=2d+1=N-1,qquad
 D\setminus T=\{P_i\to h:2\le i\le d\},qquad
 |D\setminus T|=d-1=k.
\tag{9}
\]
Every nonroot vertex has one incoming tree arrow, every vertex is reached from \(0\), and the order consisting of \(0\), then all \(P_i,Q_i\), and then \(h\) is topological.  Thus \(T\) is a rooted spanning arborescence, \(D\) is acyclic, and \(e^\star=P_1\to h\) is present.  By \(\mathrm{def:graph\mbox{-}class}\),
\[
 (G^\star_{k,N},T,e^\star)\in\mathcal G_{N,k}.
\tag{10}
\]

Choose positive rational numbers \(h_i\) and rational \(b_i\) with \(b_i^2>4h_i\), and put \(H_0=\operatorname{diag}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)\).  Choose a rational symmetric positive-definite matrix \(H\), sufficiently close to \(H_0\), with the same diagonal; a further generic restriction on its off-diagonal entries will be imposed below.  In the vertex order \((0,P_1,\ldots,P_d,Q_1,\ldots,Q_d,h)\), set
\[
 \Sigma^\star=
 \begin{pmatrix}
  1&0&0&1\\
  0&H&H&0\\
  0&H&C_0I_d&b\\
  1&0&b^{\mathsf T}&M
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad b=(b_1,\ldots,b_d)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{11}
\]
Choose rational \(C_0\) so that \(C_0I_d-H\succ0\).  The Schur complement of \(H\) in the \((P,Q)\)-principal block is \(C_0I_d-H\), so that principal block is positive definite.  Adding the independent \(0\)-coordinate preserves positive definiteness of the \((0,P,Q)\)-block.  Finally choose rational \(M\) larger than the last Schur-complement threshold.  Then
\[
 \Sigma^\star\succ0.
\tag{12}
\]

Write
\[
 a_i=\lambda_{0P_i},\qquad c_i=\lambda_{0Q_i},\qquad
 z_i=\lambda_{P_i h},\qquad z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad x=-Hz.
\]
The missing pairs are \(P_i\leftrightarrow Q_i\), \(P_i\leftrightarrow h\), and \(Q_i\leftrightarrow h\).  Direct substitution of (11) into the defining residual formula gives
\[
 0=-a_i-(Hz)_i,qquad
 0=b_i-c_i-(Hz)_i,qquad
 0=h_i+a_ic_i.
\tag{13}
\]
Since \(H\) is invertible, (13) is equivalent to
\[
 a_i=x_i,qquad c_i=x_i+b_i,qquad
 x_i^2+b_ix_i+h_i=0\quad(1\le i\le d),
 \qquad z=-H^{-1}x.
\tag{14}
\]
Each discriminant \(b_i^2-4h_i\) is positive.  Thus (14) has exactly \(2^d\) real solutions.  Under the invertible change \(z\mapsto x=-Hz\), the residual Jacobian in \((a,c,z)\) is nonsingular precisely when
\[
 det(H)\prod_{i=1}^d(2x_i+b_i)\ne0.
\tag{15}
\]
Indeed, the three equations for a fixed \(i\), expressed in \((a_i,c_i,x_i)\), have determinant up to sign \(a_i+c_i=2x_i+b_i\).  At a solution,
\[
 (2x_i+b_i)^2=b_i^2-4h_i>0,
\]
and \(\det H>0\).  Hence all \(2^d\) points are reduced.  Setting
\[
 \Omega=(I_N-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma^\star(I_N-\Lambda)
\tag{16}
\]
at any point, equations (13) make exactly the missing-pair entries vanish.  The displayed topological order makes \(I_N-\Lambda\) unit triangular and invertible, and (12) plus congruence in (16) gives \(\Omega\succ0\).  Thus all \(2^d\) solutions are real supported positive-definite source lifts.

We may choose \(H\) so that the original coefficient \(z_1=\lambda_{e^\star}\) separates the solutions.  At \(H=H_0\), branches with different \(x_1\) already have different \(z_1=-x_1/h_1\).  If two branch vectors \(x\ne x'\) have the same first coordinate, choose \(j>1\) with \(x_j\ne x'_j\) and put \(H(s)=H_0+s(E_{1j}+E_{j1})\).  Differentiating the inverse gives
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{ds}\{z_1(x)-z_1(x')\}\right|_{s=0}
 =\frac{x_j-x'_j}{h_1h_j}\ne0.
\tag{17}
\]
For each of the finitely many branch pairs, equality of their first coordinates after applying \(-H^{-1}\) is therefore a proper algebraic condition on the off-diagonal entries of \(H\).  A finite union of proper algebraic subsets cannot contain a Euclidean neighborhood of \(H_0\), and rational matrices are dense.  We choose rational \(H\) outside this union while retaining positive definiteness.  Then the \(2^d\) values of \(z_1\) are distinct.

There are \(3d\) directed coordinates and exactly \(3d\) missing residuals.  Since all other pairs are bidirected,
\[
 |D|+|B|+|V|
 =3d+\left(\binom N2-3d\right)+N
 =\frac{N(N+1)}2=:M_0.
\tag{18}
\]
Replace the independent covariance coordinates in (11) by \(\Sigma^\star+\xi\), where the \(M_0\) entries of \(\xi\) are algebraically independent.  At any reduced solution \(v_0=(a,c,z)\), seek a formal solution
\[
 v(\xi)=v_0+\sum_{r\ge1}v_r(\xi),
\]
with \(v_r\) homogeneous of degree \(r\).  The degree-\(r\) residual equation is
\[
 J(v_0)v_r=-R_r(\xi,v_1,\ldots,v_{r-1}).
\tag{19}
\]
The Jacobian is invertible by (15), so (19) determines a unique \(v_r\) recursively.  Hence every displayed point has a formal section over the full covariance formal neighborhood.

If \(f\in P_G\), substituting any such section gives \(f(\Sigma^\star+\xi)=0\) in \(\mathbb C[[\xi]]\).  Translation by \(\Sigma^\star\) is an injective automorphism of the covariance polynomial ring and the entries of \(\xi\) are algebraically independent, so \(f=0\).  Therefore
\[
 P_G=(0),\qquad K_G=\mathbb C(\sigma_{ij}:i\le j).
\tag{20}
\]
By (18), \(L\) and \(K_G\) have the same transcendence degree, so the finitely generated field extension \(L/K_G\) is finite.  Equivalently, the generic-fiber algebra \(A_K\) is a finitely generated integral algebraic \(K_G\)-algebra and hence the field \(L\).

Partition the variables into singleton blocks \(A_i=(a_i)\), singleton blocks \(C_i=(c_i)\), and one size-\(d\) block \(Z=(z_1,\ldots,z_d)\).  The residual block degrees are bounded respectively by \(A_i+C_i\), \(A_i+Z\), and \(C_i+Z\).  Thus \(\mathrm{lem:multihomogeneous\mbox{-}bezout\mbox{-}isolated\mbox{-}bound}\) gives
\[
 [L:K_G]\le
 \left[\left(\prod_{i=1}^dA_iC_i\right)Z^d\right]
 \prod_{i=1}^d(A_i+C_i)(A_i+Z)(C_i+Z)=2^d.
\tag{21}
\]
For each \(i\), exactly two selections contribute \(A_iC_iZ\), which proves the last equality.  This count applies to the original residual equations and counts multiplicity after base change to \(\overline{K_G}\).

Conversely, each formal section defines a homomorphism from the integral incidence ring into \(\mathbb C[[\xi]]\) restricting to the common injective covariance translation.  Its image has transcendence degree at least \(M_0\), equal by (18) to the dimension of the incidence domain; its prime kernel consequently has height zero and is zero.  Passing to fraction fields gives a \(K_G\)-embedding of \(L\) into \(\operatorname{Frac}\mathbb C[[\xi]]\).  The \(2^d\) embeddings send \(z_1\) to series with distinct constant terms.  Therefore the minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) over \(K_G\) has at least \(2^d\) roots, and
\[
 2^d\le[K_G(z_1):K_G]\le[L:K_G]\le2^d.
\tag{22}
\]
Thus \(d_{e^\star}(G^\star_{k,N})=2^{k+1}\), and \(e^\star\) separates all conjugate branches.  Characteristic zero makes its minimal polynomial separable.  Clearing its coefficient denominators and excluding their zeros and its nonzero discriminant leaves a nonempty Zariski-open covariance set on which these roots remain distinct; \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\) identifies them with the finite queried-coordinate projection.

For \(n>N\), append a fully bidirected child \(w\) of \(0\), place \(0\to w\) in \(T\), write \(x_w=\lambda_{0w}\), and let \(s_w\) be the new covariance row and diagonal.  No missing residual involves \(w\).  Conditional on the old source coordinates and \(x_w\), covariance congruence is an invertible triangular polynomial change between the new allowed disturbance coordinates and \(s_w\).  Hence, for the old and new fields,
\[
 L_1=L_0(x_w,s_w),\qquad K_1=K_0(s_w),
\tag{23}
\]
where \(x_w\) and the entries of \(s_w\) are algebraically independent over \(L_0\).  The minimal polynomial of \(z_1\) stays irreducible under the purely transcendental base extension \(K_0(s_w)/K_0\), so
\[
 [K_1(z_1):K_1]=[K_0(z_1):K_0]=2^d.
\tag{24}
\]
Iteration proves the degree assertion for every \(n\ge2k+4\).  Membership is preserved because each new arrow is a tree arrow and introduces no excess.  The upper bound \(D_k(n)\le2^{k+1}\) follows from \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\), while (22)--(24) give the reverse inequality.  Therefore
\[
 D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\qquad(n\ge2k+4),
\]
 with the asserted nonempty Zariski-open separation set.
body.justification: A uniform attaining region turns the exponent from a loose Bezout count into a sharp coordinate frontier for a substantial size range.
body.gap: Foygel, Draisma, and Drton already exhibit cubic and quartic behavior in small SEMs, but not an all-\(k\) family with one edge separating \(2^{k+1}\) generic branches.
body.consumer: Software maintainers obtain adversarial benchmark families and users obtain a worst-case ambiguity warning indexed by the number of added parents.
